model_claims.text: `import x as y, a` makes isort treat every module on that line as alias-only.
model_claims.source_quote: `import x as y, a` makes isort treat every module on that line as alias-only.

model_claims.text: That is harmless until the same module is also aliased somewhere else, and then the plain import disappears:
model_claims.source_quote: That is harmless until the same module is also aliased somewhere else, and then the plain import disappears:

model_claims.text:
import x as y, a
import a as b

becomes

import a as b
import x as y
model_claims.source_quote:
import x as y, a
import a as b

becomes

import a as b
import x as y

model_claims.text: Smaller forms of the same thing: `import a as b, a` and `import a, a as b` both become just `import a as b`
model_claims.source_quote: Smaller forms of the same thing: `import a as b, a` and `import a, a as b` both become just `import a as b`

model_claims.text: and with `remove_redundant_aliases=True`, `import a as a` next to `import a as b` loses the plain `import a` too.
model_claims.source_quote: and with `remove_redundant_aliases=True`, `import a as a` next to `import a as b` loses the plain `import a` too.

model_claims.text: Lazy imports behave the same way.
model_claims.source_quote: Lazy imports behave the same way.

model_claims.text: Cause: in `parse.file_contents`, `straight_import` is a single flag for the whole line. It is set to `False` as soon as the line contains an `as`, and then every module left on the line is stored with that flag, including the ones that were not aliased.
model_claims.source_quote: Cause: in `parse.file_contents`, `straight_import` is a single flag for the whole line. It is set to `False` as soon as the line contains an `as`, and then every module left on the line is stored with that flag, including the ones that were not aliased.

model_claims.text: The output only writes a plain `import a` for a module that also has aliases when that flag is `True`, so the plain import is lost.
model_claims.source_quote: The output only writes a plain `import a` for a module that also has aliases when that flag is `True`, so the plain import is lost.

model_claims.text: Fix: record which modules on the line were actually given an alias, and mark only those as alias-only. A module that is also imported bare on the same line (or whose redundant alias is removed) stays a plain import.
model_claims.source_quote: Fix: record which modules on the line were actually given an alias, and mark only those as alias-only. A module that is also imported bare on the same line (or whose redundant alias is removed) stays a plain import.

model_claims.text: From-imports are not affected; they already keep names and aliases separately.
model_claims.source_quote: From-imports are not affected; they already keep names and aliases separately.
